evidence.snippet: MGD arises due to late anaphase lag during mitosis in the zygote, although Y chromosomal abnormalities are sometimes seen and interchromosomal rearrangement occurs.
evidence.explanation: Reviews the proposed chromosomal origin rather than documenting the embryonic event in the cohort.

steps/0.description: Early post-zygotic Y-chromosome loss, for example through mitotic anaphase lag, can generate a 45,X lineage alongside Y-bearing cells. Structural Y abnormalities may also be involved. The resulting mosaicism is a chromosomal event, with variable distribution among tissues.

evidence.snippet: In the mixed gonadal dysgenesis cases (cases 3 and 4), the testis had a higher percentage (greater than two fold) of XY cells than the ovary had.
evidence.explanation: Direct human tissue evidence in two cases, not a universal ratio or developmental threshold.

evidence.snippet: The average percentages of 45,X cells of this patient's gonad and a control testis were 39.0% and 5.7%, respectively (χ2 test, P < 0.001).
evidence.explanation: Digital FISH analysis of one resected gonad supports tissue mosaicism, with a nonzero false-negative background in the control.

steps/1.description: 45,X and Y-bearing cell lineages vary between blood and gonadal tissue and among gonadal cell populations. Human gonadal FISH has directly measured this mosaicism. Two MGD cases in a five-person study had higher XY fractions in testicular than streak ovarian tissue; a separate case had gonadal mosaicism despite a 46,XY blood karyotype. These postnatal observations do not define the embryonic threshold for testis differentiation.

evidence.snippet: Short stature is a common clinical feature in individuals with MGD and is typically attributed to the 45,X cell line, and associated haploinsufficiency of the SHOX gene
evidence.explanation: Attributes the short stature to SHOX dosage in the 45,X lineage, which is what this node asserts.

steps/2.description: Cells of the 45,X lineage carry one copy of the pseudoautosomal SHOX gene rather than the usual two copies. This provides a plausible contribution to impaired skeletal growth, while tissue mosaicism and other endocrine or chromosomal factors can also influence stature. SHOX dosage does not explain all Turner-associated cardiac, renal or autoimmune findings.

evidence.snippet: Of 34 patients with 45,X/46,XY mosaicism, a unilateral dysgenetic testis and a contralateral streak gonad was detected in 20 patients (59%), bilateral streak gonads in 9 (26%), and bilateral dysgenetic testes in 5 (15%).
evidence.explanation: Reports histologic distributions in a surgically selected cohort, not population frequencies.

evidence.snippet: A gonad composed of both streak and dysgenetic testicular portions was observed in 7 gonads of 6 patients.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates intragonadal histologic heterogeneity without identifying its embryonic cause.

evidence.snippet: typically characterised by the presence of a dysgenetic testis at various levels of descent on one side and a streak gonad on the other
evidence.explanation: The canonical description of the asymmetric anatomy.

steps/3.description: Gonadal tissue may include a streak gonad, dysgenetic testis, or apparently normal testis. The characteristic contralateral streak/testis combination is not universal: a selected 34-patient biopsy/gonadectomy series also included bilateral streaks and bilateral dysgenetic testes, and some individual gonads contained both streak and testicular portions.

evidence.snippet: AMH concentrations in individuals with MGD are typically toward the lower end of the reference range for healthy male infants with normal testicular function, reflecting relative Sertoli cell dysfunction
evidence.explanation: Describes impaired secretion rather than a measured loss of Sertoli cell mass.

steps/4.description: AMH secretion by dysgenetic Sertoli-cell tissue can be reduced, with concentrations often toward the lower end of the typical male infant range. The degree of dysfunction varies; a universal reduction in Sertoli cell number has not been established by the cited clinical measurements.

evidence.snippet: Due to the presence of dysgenetic testis, the plasma testosterone concentrations in MGD patients tend to be low‐normal relative to typical male infants but remain elevated compared with those typically seen in female infants.
evidence.explanation: Supports a relative and variable secretory deficit.

steps/5.description: Leydig-cell steroidogenic function can be reduced in dysgenetic testes. Basal and stimulated testosterone values vary with age and retained gonadal tissue. Reduced fetal androgen exposure contributes to incomplete external genital virilization; later androgen insufficiency may require replacement.

evidence.snippet: 71% (n = 5) of those evaluated at the end of puberty presented signs of declined Sertoli cell function (low inhibin B levels and increased FSH levels)
evidence.explanation: Five individuals in the evaluated end-of-puberty subset had this biochemical pattern.

steps/6.description: Low inhibin B and rising FSH indicate impaired Sertoli-cell function in some individuals during or after puberty. Spontaneous pubertal onset and Sertoli dysfunction can coexist; gonadotropin or inhibin measurements do not by themselves demonstrate universal Leydig-cell failure.

evidence.snippet: Twenty-five percent had focal spermatogenesis, and another 25.0% had arrested spermatogenesis.
evidence.explanation: Histologic observations in the assessed subset of a 63-person multicenter male cohort; the abstract does not fully resolve the denominator for each histologic percentage.

steps/7.description: Germ-cell maturation is impaired in some dysgenetic testes. A multicenter male cohort found both focal and arrested spermatogenesis, while some men retained motile sperm. Histologic observations and semen results came from different assessed subsets; neither establishes complete absence of fertility potential throughout the mosaic population.

evidence.snippet: Many individuals have Müllerian remnants on the same side as the streak gonad, whereas the most common phenotypic finding is proximal hypospadias with perineal division of the corpus spongiosum and ventral curvature
evidence.explanation: Reports the anatomic association, without establishing a unique mode of hormone action.

steps/8.description: Incomplete fetal regression of Müllerian derivatives can leave a uterus or hemi-uterus, fallopian tube remnant, or prostatic utricle. Remnants are often ipsilateral to the streak gonad. This anatomic association is compatible with variable local AMH action but does not, by itself, prove that AMH acts exclusively locally or exclude systemic hormone effects.

evidence.snippet: The GBY candidate genes DDX3Y and TSPY are expressed in the germ cells of DSD-XY patients from distinct etiologies: patients with mixed gonadal dysgenesis (MGD) and sex chromosome mosaics (45,X0/46,XY; 46,XX/46,XY)
evidence.explanation: Patient-tissue expression supports candidate involvement, with nonmalignant expression limiting causal interpretation.

evidence.snippet: This suggest that GBY candidate proteins are also expressed in the non-malignant germ cells of DSD-XY individuals like in male spermatogonia.
evidence.explanation: Patient-tissue expression supports candidate involvement, with nonmalignant expression limiting causal interpretation.

evidence.snippet: For individuals with 45,X/46,XY mosaicism, the lifetime risk of developing gonadal tumours is estimated at 15%–25%, with this risk rising with age, although the true incidence may be confounded by the historical practice of early gonadectomy and diagnostic challenges
evidence.explanation: The review qualifies its estimated tumour risk by prior surgery and diagnostic uncertainty.

evidence.snippet: Pathologic examination revealed gonadal tumors in 6 of the 34 (18%) patients, including a gonadoblastoma in 7 gonads among 5 patients and an association of dysgerminoma with gonadoblastoma in 1 gonad.
evidence.explanation: Reports co-occurring gonadoblastoma and dysgerminoma in a resection specimen, not longitudinal observation of progression.

evidence.snippet: Among Group I patients, the 4 dysgenetic testes affected by CIS in 3 patients were intraabdominal (n=1), inguinal (n=1) and scrotal (n=2) in positions.
evidence.explanation: In-situ lesions occurred in scrotal as well as inguinal and abdominal testes; position alone does not exclude neoplasia.

steps/9.description: Gonadoblastoma or germ cell neoplasia in situ can occur in dysgenetic gonads containing Y material, and invasive germ cell tumours are also reported. Risk estimates vary with phenotype, age, gonadal histology, ascertainment and prior gonadectomy. TSPY and DDX3Y are candidate susceptibility genes expressed in affected germ cells, but their expression also occurs in nonmalignant cells and does not establish sufficiency for transformation.

evidence.snippet: The clinical spectrum of MGD to an extent is influenced by the functional capacity of the dysgenetic gonad along with the degree of androgen exposure during critical periods of foetal development
evidence.explanation: Ties the degree of virilization to androgen exposure during the fetal window.

steps/10.description: Variable androgen exposure during fetal development contributes to atypical external genital anatomy, including hypospadias and ventral curvature. The wider mosaicism spectrum also includes typical external genitalia; the mechanism is not present to the same degree in every individual.

evidence.snippet: The phenotypic presentation of MGD varies from atypical genitalia to typical male or female appearances often associated with Turner stigmata.
evidence.explanation: Describes the full external phenotypic range. No frequency band: the cohort denominators available count patients ascertained in different ways, and the mildest presentations are by definition under-ascertained.

steps/11.description: Atypical external genital appearance is a common reason for diagnosis, while other individuals with the same mosaic karyotype have typical male or female genitalia.

evidence.snippet: the most common phenotypic finding is proximal hypospadias with perineal division of the corpus spongiosum and ventral curvature
evidence.explanation: Names it as the commonest external genital finding.

steps/12.description: Proximal hypospadias may have a perineal or scrotal meatus; not every proximal lesion is perineal.

evidence.snippet: Many individuals have Müllerian remnants on the same side as the streak gonad
evidence.explanation: Reports the finding and its characteristic laterality.

steps/13.description: Retained uterine or hemi-uterine tissue and fallopian-tube remnants can occur, often on the streak-gonad side. Persistence is not unique to MGD and also occurs in other gonadal dysgeneses.

evidence.snippet: Testicular insufficiency develops in 60%–70% of individuals raised as males by the third decade, and infertility is the most commonly reported outcome.
evidence.explanation: Names infertility as the commonest outcome. No frequency band: "most commonly reported outcome" ranks it against other outcomes rather than giving a proportion of patients.

evidence.snippet: Fourteen out of 17 (82%) with semen analyses were azoospermic; three had motile sperm.
evidence.explanation: The tested subgroup supports severe but not universal spermatogenic impairment.

steps/14.description: Impaired spermatogenesis and infertility are frequent clinical concerns. Fertility potential is variable rather than absent in all individuals; three of 17 men undergoing semen analysis in one multicenter cohort had motile sperm.

evidence.snippet: Most patients had stunted growth, with abnormal growth spurt during puberty and a mean adult height of 158 ± 7.6 cm, i.e. -2.3 DS with correction for target height.
evidence.explanation: Gives the adult height and its standard-deviation deficit against target height.

evidence.snippet: height Z-score was significantly decreased with age for both genders (p = 0.02)
evidence.explanation: Confirms the progressive nature of the height deficit in an independent cohort.

evidence.snippet: Short stature is common in individuals regardless of their phenotypic sex.
evidence.explanation: States that short stature is common and independent of phenotypic sex.

steps/15.description: Height Z-score falls progressively through childhood, mirroring the Turner syndrome growth trajectory. In a French series of boys with normal or near-normal genitalia, mean adult height was 158 cm.

evidence.snippet: Pathologic examination revealed gonadal tumors in 6 of the 34 (18%) patients, including a gonadoblastoma in 7 gonads among 5 patients and an association of dysgerminoma with gonadoblastoma in 1 gonad.
